transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you. Well, I guess what finally pushed me to come in is that I just can’t seem to organize all the moving parts anymore. There's a lot going on right now—patent notes, workshop prep, gallery deadlines, team decisions—and I just can't seem to keep it all straight. 

Instead of prioritizing, I end up just starting whatever is loudest at the moment, instead of focusing on what actually matters. It's really starting to become a problem for me.
Have you struggled with organization and focus for most of your life, including childhood, or is this a more recent change?

No, it's not a recent change. Looking back... this was definitely there in grade school, too. I remember my teachers used to write on my report cards that I was bright, but that I daydreamed a lot. I'd forget to turn in assignments that I had actually finished, or... I'd just lose my homework folders completely. So, yeah, this has been an issue since long before I was a teenager.
Do you find yourself constantly overwhelmed by persistent, uncontrollable worry about everyday things?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I definitely get stressed out when I'm falling behind on my projects or when I drop the ball on something important, but... I don't really have that kind of constant worry about everyday things. It's not so much an anxious feeling as it is just... being frustrated and overwhelmed by the actual mess I've made of my schedule.
